method_name: Unified VOS (Variable and Operator Splitting) Framework
definition: A framework that derives Nesterov's accelerated method and ADMM from a common continuous-time ODE: X'' + gamma(t)*X' + grad_f(X) = 0
assumptions: f is convex with L-Lipschitz continuous gradient
g is convex (possibly non-smooth) with computable proximal operator
For linear convergence: f is mu-strongly convex (mu > 0)
invariants: Lyapunov function E(t) is monotonically non-increasing along trajectories
For strongly convex case: E(t) <= E(0)*exp(-sqrt(mu)*t)
For general convex case: f(X(t)) - f* <= C/t^2
non_negotiable_structural_steps: 1. Start from continuous-time ODE with damping
2. Variable splitting: introduce velocity V = X'
3. Operator splitting: decompose f + g with auxiliary variables
4. Discretize to obtain Nesterov (variable splitting) or ADMM (operator splitting)
5. Construct Lyapunov function to prove convergence rate
key_distinguishing_features: Unifies acceleration and splitting through common ODE
Phase transition at damping constant r=3
Lyapunov function combines objective gap with kinetic energy
Momentum coefficient derived from condition number: beta = (sqrt(kappa)-1)/(sqrt(kappa)+1)
deviations_from_ideal: VOS-ADMM acceleration not fully converged - needs more sophisticated acceleration strategy
Lasso problem has mu~0, so linear convergence verified only on auxiliary quadratic problem
